candidates.exact_span: Any notice shall include information on (i) the quality and quantity of effluent to be introduced into the treatment works, and (ii) any anticipated impact of the change on the quality or quantity of effluent to be discharged from the POTW.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Interpretation of what changes trigger notice, and how effluent quality/quantity or discharge impacts are documented, can change whether conditional monitoring or reporting obligations were applicable and how missing or anticipated-change evidence is classified.

candidates.exact_span: The permittee shall operate an industrial pretreatment program in accordance with Section 402(b)(8) of the Clean Water Act, the General Pretreatment Regulations (40 CFR Part 403) and the approved POTW pretreatment program submitted by the permittee.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Different readings of which external authorities and approved program documents govern the permittee's obligations could change which numeric pretreatment standards, monitoring requirements, and missing-evidence rules are treated as applicable for FY2025.

candidates.exact_span: The POTW pretreatment program is hereby incorporated by reference and shall be implemented in a manner consistent with the following requirements:
candidates.computation_change_reason: What counts as incorporated by reference, and what 'consistent with the following requirements' adds beyond the referenced program, can change which limits, monitoring duties, and no-data explanations are sourced from the permit versus external program text.

candidates.exact_span: Industrial user information shall be updated at a frequency adequate to ensure that all IUs are properly characterized at all times;
candidates.computation_change_reason: The open-ended standard 'adequate' frequency and 'properly characterized' can change whether characterization or update monitoring was required for a given period and whether absent IU information is a documented no-data state or unresolved missing evidence.

candidates.exact_span: The frequency and nature of industrial user compliance monitoring activities by the permittee shall be commensurate with the character, consistency and volume of waste.
candidates.computation_change_reason: How 'commensurate' is applied to waste character, consistency, and volume can change which compliance monitoring activities were required and whether a missing result reflects conditional non-requirement or inadequate evidence.

candidates.exact_span: The permittee must inspect and sample the effluent from each Significant Industrial User in accordance with 40 CFR 403.8(f)(2)(v). This is in addition to any industrial self-monitoring activities;
candidates.computation_change_reason: Interpretation of who qualifies as a Significant Industrial User and what 403.8(f)(2)(v) requires can change applicable POTW monitoring obligations; the self-monitoring carve-out affects whether missing data is attributed to POTW duties, IU self-monitoring, or unresolved gaps.

candidates.exact_span: The permittee shall enforce and obtain remedies for noncompliance by any industrial users with applicable pretreatment standards and requirements;
candidates.computation_change_reason: Which pretreatment standards and requirements are treated as 'applicable' to industrial users can change the enforceable numeric limits considered in compliance comparisons and the monitoring tied to demonstrating compliance or noncompliance.

candidates.exact_span: The permittee shall control through permit, order, or similar means, the contribution to the POTW by each Industrial User to ensure compliance with applicable Pretreatment Standards and Requirements. In the case of Industrial Users identified as significant under 40 CFR 403.3(v), this control shall be achieved through individual or general control mechanisms, in accordance with
candidates.computation_change_reason: Scope of 'Pretreatment Standards and Requirements,' significance under 403.3(v), and the type of control mechanism can change which numeric limits apply, which monitoring conditions are embedded in permits/orders, and whether absent results reflect conditional non-requirement or missing required evidence.
